title: SharpaOpenData Episode Schema
description: Describes the on-disk format of a SINGLE episode of the SharpaOpenData dataset stored at /mnt/netdata/Team/Academic/Data/North/SharpaOpenData. An episode is one directory containing exactly one HDF5 file (all robot sensor / actuator time series) plus JSON sidecar files (human annotations and provenance). This document is descriptive: it is a JSON-Schema-flavoured spec of the directory, the HDF5 tree and the sidecar JSON files. It was derived by inspecting the actual data (56 task collections, ~30k episodes, 50 tasks structurally sampled).

dataset_layout.description: Directory hierarchy above a single episode. Most tasks use 3 levels; the `easy10` collection inserts an extra sub-task level.
notes: `ROBOT_ID` (e.g. POC22027, POC22007, POC22054) identifies the physical robot / collection station.
A `season_*` directory groups all episodes recorded in one continuous collection session. Its timestamp equals the timestamp of its first episode.
The season directory also contains a `train.json` manifest and, usually, a `lerobotv2.1_clean/` LeRobot v2.1 export of the same episodes. See `sibling_artifacts` below.

<basic_tag>@<timestamp>.hdf5.description: The episode payload. Filename pattern `train_0.3.0@YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS.hdf5`, where `train_0.3.0` is the SDK/basic tag and the timestamp matches the parent episode directory. Exactly one per episode.

temporal_model.description: Every dataset in the file is a time series whose FIRST axis is time. There are exactly two clock rates, and understanding the distinction is essential.

aligned_rate.description: The canonical episode timeline, locked to the head-camera shutter. ALL `observe/**` datasets and ALL `mode/**` datasets have first dimension N. Every `startStep`/`endStep`/`start`/`end` index appearing in the JSON sidecars is an index into this timeline, inclusive on both ends, valid in [0, N-1].

raw_rate.relation: M == 2 * N (verified exactly on all sampled episodes; may be off by one on rare episodes)
raw_rate.description: The proprioception control loop rate. ALL `state/**` and `action/**` value datasets (`joint_angle`, `joint_effort`, `tcp_pose`, `velocity`, ...) have first dimension M, i.e. they are recorded at double the video rate.

aligned_index.description: The bridge between the two rates: `aligned_index[k]` is the row in the 60 Hz arrays of the same group that corresponds to aligned frame `k`. Monotonically non-decreasing; in practice `aligned_index[k] == 2*k`. To build a 30 Hz-synchronised training sample at frame k, index images/tactile/mode directly with `k`, and index proprioception with `aligned_index[k]`.

columns.name: timestamp
columns.description: Absolute UNIX wall-clock timestamp (e.g. 1776482492.xx). This is the only column carrying information.

columns.name: valid
columns.description: Observed to be constant 1.0 across every `time` dataset in every sampled episode. Treat as a validity flag and ignore.

time.raw_time_note: `raw_time` (present on `mode`, `state/chassis`, `action/chassis`, `observe/imu`) is the pre-synchronisation sensor timestamp; `time` is the post-synchronisation timestamp. Prefer `time`.

embodiment.description: A stationary/wheeled bimanual humanoid with two 7-DoF arms, two 22-DoF dexterous hands, a 7-DoF auxiliary `motor` chain, an optional 2-DoF chassis, 4 RGB cameras and 10 fingertip tactile sensors. The DoF counts are identical across all 50 structurally sampled tasks.

motor.description: Auxiliary body chain (head / neck / torso actuators). Named only positionally in the official LeRobot export.

chassis.description: Mobile base, [linear, angular] velocity. Optional and usually all-zero for tabletop tasks.

embodiment.name_source: Joint naming taken verbatim from the sibling LeRobot export `lerobotv2.1_clean/meta/info.json`, whose 65-D `observation.state` vector is the concatenation [left_arm(7), left_hand(22), right_arm(7), right_hand(22), motor(7)].

state.description: Measured proprioception (what the robot actually did). Sampled at 60 Hz -> first dim M.

tcp_pose.description: End-effector pose [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] (position in m, rotation as rotation-vector/Euler in rad). NOTE: observed to be all-zero on some collections (e.g. ClearPlate) - always check for a non-zero norm before using.

tcp_force.description: End-effector wrench [fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz].

tcp_forces.description: IDENTICAL SEMANTICS to `tcp_force`; older collections use the plural spelling. A reader MUST accept either name: `g.get('tcp_force', g.get('tcp_forces'))`. The two never co-occur.

velocity.description: [linear, angular]. One sampled task uses 3 components. Typically all-zero for stationary tabletop tasks.

action.description: Commanded targets (what the teleoperator/controller asked for). Same 60 Hz timeline and same layout as `state`, but only positional commands are recorded. This is the supervision signal for behaviour cloning.

observe.description: Exteroception. Everything here is on the 30 Hz aligned timeline -> first dim N.

vision.description: Four RGB streams. Each stream is a group with a `rgb` blob dataset and a `time` dataset. There are NO depth streams in this dataset.

encoding.description: CRITICAL: `rgb` is NOT a decoded image array. It is a 2-D uint8 matrix of shape (N, PAD) holding one ZERO-PADDED JPEG bytestream per row, where PAD is the largest JPEG in that episode/stream. Row length is constant; actual payload length varies per frame.
encoding.decode_recipe: buf = rgb[k].tobytes(); buf = buf[:buf.rfind(b'\xff\xd9') + 2]; img = PIL.Image.open(io.BytesIO(buf))
encoding.decode_note: Trim at the JPEG EOI marker `FFD9` rather than trimming trailing zeros, since valid JPEG data can contain 0x00 bytes.

jpeg_deep_encoded.description: Marks the row as a padded JPEG bytestream.

crop_roi.description: Region of interest within the frame recommended by the collection pipeline. Advisory metadata; the stored JPEG is the FULL uncropped frame.

jpeg_quality.description: JPEG quality factor used at encode time.

time.description: This stream's `time[:,0]` defines the canonical episode timeline.

head/stereo/righteye.description: Second eye of the head stereo pair. Same encoding; `crop_roi` present on only some collections (30/50).

left_wrist/fisheye | right_wrist/fisheye.description: Wrist-mounted fisheye cameras, downscaled at write time.

tactile.description: Ten vision-based fingertip tactile sensors, one group per finger. Always present in full (10/10 fingers, 50/50 tasks).

force.description: Resultant contact force [fx, fy, fz] at the fingertip.

torque.description: Resultant contact torque [tx, ty, tz] at the fingertip.

raw.description: Raw tactile sensor camera image, 320 x 240 GRAYSCALE, stored as a zero-padded JPEG bytestream (same decode recipe as `vision/**/rgb`).

deform.description: Derived gel-deformation / contact map, 240 x 240 GRAYSCALE, stored as a zero-padded JPEG bytestream. Much smaller than `raw` (~1 KB vs ~20 KB per frame); near-uniform when the finger is not in contact.

imu.presence: 2/50 tasks - rare, do not depend on it

aligned_orientation.description: Quaternion re-referenced to the episode start frame.

mode.description: Per-frame robot operating mode on the 30 Hz aligned timeline. Present in 49/50 tasks.

operation_mode.description: Control mode of the session. Observed constant 0 across every sampled episode (teleoperation).

state.description: Top-level robot state. Observed constant 2 across every sampled episode (recording/running).

sub_state.description: Phase within the episode. VERIFIED to correspond exactly to the annotation segments: 1 = task execution (frame-for-frame identical to the `valid` segment in anno.json), 2 = homing / return-to-rest (frame-for-frame identical to the `home` segment). Filtering to `sub_state == 1` is an annotation-free way to drop the trailing homing motion.
